newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hariri wants 30-year $1 bln bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hariri wants 30-year $1 bln bond issue.

text.p: Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has proposed that Lebanon make a 30-year dollar-denominated treasury bond issue to finance emergency social spending.

Hariri proposed a $1 billion issue at a Wednesday night cabinet meeting. Newspapers said the proposal caused an uproar and two cabinet ministers walked out saying it would impose an intolerable tax burden on the country.
Lebanon currently issues dollar-denominated treasury bills and bonds ranging from six months to two years.

Beirut financiers say the government has been preparing to issue three-year bonds for some time, but there has been no previous mention of 30-year bonds. If eventually approved by the cabinet, the proposal would require passage of a law by parliament.
Banking sources told Reuters the proposal was worked out at a recent meeting between Hariri, President Elias Hrawi, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh and acting finance minister Fouad Siniora.
"It was prepared in a very secretive way at a meeting between them last week on this issue," a banker said. "I have a feeling it will be sold in the United States mainly," he said.
